content.caseIdentity: Lloyd v. Grace, Smith & Co., [1912] AC 716 (House of Lords)
content.holding: A firm of solicitors was held vicariously liable for the fraud of their managing clerk who induced a client to transfer her property to him, even though the clerk acted entirely for his own benefit and without the knowledge of the partners.
content.relevance: Established that a master is liable for the fraudulent acts of a servant committed in the course of employment.
